findings: render_all.sh script complexity increased from ~10 to 201 lines to implement output-based chunk judgment, sweep passes, and outcome recording. This complexity is necessary for the crash tolerance features and is explicitly allowed by the spec requirement 'Bash for the wrapper shell'. The script is well-structured with a clear worker function and maintains single responsibility (chunk-based parallel rendering with crash tolerance).

render_stats.py adds environment-dependent path resolution (VIDEO_CONTENT_DIR and rglob search) to support both production and test contexts. This is necessary for the spec's deterministic test requirement (tests without real Blender) and maintains production path as the default. Complexity is justified by test infrastructure needs.

Changes align with Decision 0002 (Headless Blender for modeled 3D assets) by making the Blender render wrapper more robust and reliable. Output-based chunk judgment and crash tolerance directly address the intermittent Blender exit crashes while preserving deterministic build behavior.

Frozen surfaces respected: no changes to scene scripts (film.py, scene_*.py, common.py, etc.), stations, pipelines, or review contracts. Changes are isolated to production tooling (render_all.sh and render_stats.py).

Project style rules followed: no em or en dashes in produced files, Python code uses standard library only, compatibility contracts preserved (invocation, frame naming, log naming, SECTION_RENDER_DONE format).
Test infrastructure properly structured: deterministic tests in tests/ directory drive wrapper with fake Blender via BLENDER environment variable, following established factory test patterns.
